title: Reducing Dishes
summary: A chef has recorded the satisfaction levels of n dishes, each taking exactly 1 unit of time to prepare.
statement: A chef has recorded the satisfaction levels of n dishes, each taking exactly 1 unit of time to prepare. The like-time coefficient for a dish is calculated as the product of the time taken to prepare that dish (including all previous dishes) and its satisfaction level. Determine the maximum possible sum of these like-time coefficients by choosing any order of preparation or discarding some dishes.
constraints: Choose and arrange any dishes; a dish at one-based time t contributes t*satisfaction.
Return the maximum total, allowing zero by cooking no dishes.
hints: An optimal chosen order is ascending satisfaction.
Build that order backward from the largest value.
Prepending changes the total by the sum of all included values plus the new value.
Continue exactly while this gain is positive; smaller later candidates cannot recover after it fails.
editorial: Continue exactly while this gain is positive; smaller later candidates cannot recover after it fails.

tests.explanation: Cooking -1, 0, and 5 in order yields the maximum 14.
All positive dishes are used in ascending order for total 20.
